---

# Japan, first time — ten days, two people, November 2026

**Tokyo → Hakone → Kyoto → Nara → Osaka.** Nine nights on the ground, open-jaw flights, no rail pass. **~¥536,000 (~$3,420) for two** before international airfare. Rate used: ¥157 = $1.

## Three structural decisions

**Fly open-jaw: into Haneda, home out of Kansai.** Usually costs the same as a round trip and saves a wasted ¥28,000 backtrack plus half a day. Book as one multi-city ticket, not two one-ways.

**Skip the Japan Rail Pass.** This is the big money question and the answer is clearly no. From 1 October 2026 the 7-day ordinary pass is ¥53,000 per person. This itinerary's long-distance rail is about ¥14,000 per person. The pass made sense at ¥29,650; on a Golden Route trip in 2026 it's roughly a ¥78,000 mistake for two. Buy singles.

**Suggested dates: Fri 13 – Sun 22 November.** Kyoto's colour peaks roughly 20 Nov – 7 Dec, later than most people assume, and 2026 signals point slightly later than average. But peak colour also means crushing crowds and rooms 30–40% over baseline. This window puts you in Kyoto 18–21 Nov — early peak, with the higher ground already turning — and on Wed/Thu/Fri rather than a weekend, which matters enormously at Kiyomizu-dera.

- Avoid if you shift: **3 Nov** (Culture Day, Tuesday) and **23 Nov** (Labour Thanksgiving, Monday — a 21–23 Nov long weekend). Your last night, Sat 21 Nov in Osaka, clips the front of it; book early and it's fine since Osaka isn't a foliage destination.
- **Cheaper alternative: 6–15 November.** Trade peak Kyoto colour for lower rates, thinner crowds, and better Hakone foliage (which peaks earlier, at altitude). Saves roughly $250.

---

## Day by day

### Day 1 — Fri 13 Nov · Tokyo · Land, don't be ambitious
- Haneda → city on **Keikyu** (¥300 pp to Shinagawa, 15 min) or the **Monorail** (¥520 pp). Both beat the ¥1,400 limousine bus unless you're wrecked.
- Set up your IC card *before* leaving the airport (details below).
- Stay in one neighbourhood. From a Shinjuku base: Omoide Yokochō and Golden Gai for the alleys, a bowl of ramen, early night.

> Jet lag hits hardest on nights 2 and 3, not night 1. Plan the easiest day for Day 3.

### Day 2 — Sat 14 Nov · Tokyo · West side
- **Meiji Jingū at opening (~6:15am).** Cedar-lined approach, essentially empty at dawn. The single best use of your jet lag.
- Takeshita-dōri for spectacle, Omotesandō for architecture and department-store food halls.
- Shibuya Crossing, then **Shibuya Sky** at sunset (~¥2,700 pp, timed entry, **book a month out** — golden-hour slots go first).
- Dinner: izakaya in Shibuya or Ebisu.

> It's a Saturday. Harajuku and Shibuya hit maximum density around 1pm. Front-load the morning.

### Day 3 — Sun 15 Nov · Tokyo · Old Tokyo
- **Sensō-ji, Asakusa, early.** Grounds are open 24h; Nakamise shops open ~9. Being there at 7am is a different experience entirely.
- **Kappabashi** kitchen-supply street — knives, ceramics, plastic food. One of Tokyo's best shopping streets, nearly tour-group-free.
- Sumida River walk toward Skytree.
- Afternoon: Ueno Park and the **Tokyo National Museum** (¥1,000 pp) — the best single museum in the country for context on everything you'll see in Kyoto.
- Evening: Yanaka's low-rise lanes, or Akihabara.

### Day 4 — Mon 16 Nov · Tokyo · Market, digital art, modern city
- **Tsukiji Outer Market** for breakfast at 8am — tamagoyaki, uni, tuna skewers. No booking.
- **teamLab Borderless** at Azabudai Hills (~¥3,800 pp, timed, **book 3–4 weeks out**). Take the earliest slot; the rooms are small and the experience collapses when crowded.
- Zōjō-ji and Tokyo Tower, or the free Imperial Palace East Gardens.
- Last Tokyo dinner — the night to spend on a proper sushi counter or Ginza yakitori.

> **Swap:** **Kamakura** is 1h and ¥940 each way (Great Buddha, Hase-dera, temple hiking trails). **Nikkō** is grander but 2h each way, and by mid-November its best foliage is gone.
> **Don't plan on the Ghibli Museum** — closed for renovation 1 Oct 2026 to mid-April 2027.

### Day 5 — Tue 17 Nov · Tokyo → Hakone · Mountains and a proper onsen
- **First: forward your big bags to the Kyoto hotel** via the front desk (takkyubin, ~¥2,300/case, next-day). Overnight bag only to Hakone. Best logistics move of the trip — the Hakone loop is five vehicle changes, several of them small.
- **Odakyu Romancecar, Shinjuku → Hakone-Yumoto**, ~85 min. Reserve seats (¥1,200 pp surcharge); front-row observation seats sell out.
- The loop counter-clockwise, all on the Freepass: Tozan switchback railway → Gōra → cable car → **ropeway over Ōwakudani** (volcanic vents, black eggs, the Fuji view) → pirate boat across Lake Ashi → the torii standing in the water at Hakone Shrine.
- Ryokan by 5pm. Onsen, kaiseki dinner in yukata, onsen again.

> Fuji is visible maybe half of winter mornings and much less in the afternoon. If it's out at Ōwakudani, stop and look properly — don't assume tomorrow.

### Day 6 — Wed 18 Nov · Hakone → Kyoto
- Morning onsen, then the **Hakone Open-Air Museum** (¥1,600 pp) — Moore and Picasso in a mountain valley, with a foot bath. 5 minutes from Gōra.
- Down to Odawara for a ~12:30 **Hikari shinkansen to Kyoto** (~2h05, ¥12,320 pp reserved). Nozomi doesn't stop at Odawara; Hikari is the right train and barely slower on this leg.
- Arrive ~14:45. Your forwarded luggage is waiting.
- Evening: **Nishiki Market** before ~6pm, then Pontochō alley and Gion's Hanamikōji at dusk, ending at Yasaka Shrine (lit, open late).

> Buy an ekiben and a beer at Odawara station before boarding. Not a formality — there's nothing worth having on board.

### Day 7 — Thu 19 Nov · Kyoto · Eastern hills, from dawn
- **Kiyomizu-dera at 6:00am opening** (¥500 pp). Non-negotiable in foliage season — at 6am you have the veranda nearly to yourselves; by 10am the approach is shoulder-to-shoulder.
- Down through **Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka** before the shops open, then Kōdai-ji and Maruyama Park.
- Chion-in's colossal gate, then lunch.
- Afternoon: **Nanzen-ji** (free grounds, brick aqueduct, ¥600 garden) → **Philosopher's Path** → **Ginkaku-ji** (¥500 pp). This stretch is where Kyoto's maples are best in the third week of November.
- Evening: **Eikan-dō illumination** (¥600–1,000, mid-Nov to early Dec, no booking — expect a queue).

> Kyoto's buses are the city's weak point in November — slow, crowded, cash-fiddly. Use the subway where it goes, take taxis freely for short hops (¥800–1,500 across most of the east side, split two ways it beats the bus on time), walk the rest.

### Day 8 — Fri 20 Nov · Kyoto · West and north, plus a shrine after dark
- **Arashiyama bamboo grove at 7:30am.** Short, narrow path — magical empty, miserable at midday. Early or not at all.
- **Tenryū-ji** garden (¥500 pp), then Ōkōchi Sansō villa (¥1,000 pp, includes matcha, half as crowded as everything nearby).
- Optional: **Sagano Romantic Train** along the gorge (¥880 pp) — **book ahead**, sells out completely in foliage season.
- Afternoon: **Kinkaku-ji** (¥500 pp — 30 minutes, one view, worth it) and **Ryōan-ji**'s rock garden (¥600 pp).
- **Evening: Fushimi Inari after dark.** Open 24h, free, lit. The torii tunnels at 8pm with almost nobody in them are the best hour you'll spend in Kyoto. 2 hours for the full mountain loop, 45 min for the lower gates.

### Day 9 — Sat 21 Nov · Kyoto → Nara → Osaka
- Forward bags Kyoto hotel → Osaka hotel before 10am (~¥1,600/case). Travel light.
- **Kintetsu limited express, Kyoto → Nara**, ~35 min, ¥1,160 pp — arrives at the edge of the park.
- **Tōdai-ji** (¥800 pp) — largest bronze Buddha in one of the largest wooden buildings on earth; the scale doesn't photograph. Then the deer park and **Kasuga Taisha**'s three thousand stone lanterns.
- Lunch and a wander in **Naramachi**, the old merchant quarter.
- ~4pm: **Kintetsu Nara → Osaka-Namba**, 45 min, ¥680 pp.
- Evening: **Dōtonbori** neon, then eat properly — okonomiyaki, kushikatsu (don't double-dip the sauce), takoyaki. Shinsekai for the rougher, better version.

> The deer bow for crackers and will mug you for a paper map. Keep loose food out of open bags.

### Day 10 — Sun 22 Nov · Osaka → home
- Depending on your flight: **Osaka Castle** park (free grounds, ¥600 keep), the **Umeda Sky Building** observatory (¥2,000 pp), or a last run at Kuromon Market.
- **Nankai Namba → Kansai Airport**, 45 min, ¥970 pp on the airport express (¥1,490 pp for the Rapi:t with reserved seats).
- Be at KIX **3 hours** early — check-in queues for US-bound carriers are long.

## Where to stay

**Tokyo — 4 nights, ~¥22,000/night.** **Shinjuku** is the right first-timer base: the Odakyu line to Hakone leaves from here and it's on the Yamanote loop. Look at business-hotel chains — Sotetsu Fresa Inn, Mitsui Garden, Hotel Gracery, Tokyu Stay. Small rooms, spotless, excellent value. Alternatives: Marunouchi/Tokyo Station (calmer, better for the shinkansen) or Asakusa (cheaper, more atmospheric, less central). Avoid Roppongi unless nightlife is the point.

**Hakone — 1 night, ~¥45,000 for two.** The one deliberate splurge, and it should be a **ryokan with an onsen and half board** — which offsets a day of food costs. Stay in **Gōra** or **Sengokuhara** (better views, on the loop) rather than Hakone-Yumoto. If either of you has tattoos, filter for a room with a private open-air bath (*kashikiri* / *rotenburo-tsuki*) — worth it regardless. **Book this first**; good ryokan sell out for November months ahead.

**Kyoto — 3 nights, ~¥28,000/night.** The tightest, most expensive booking. **Karasuma/Shijō** is the sweet spot — subway on both lines, walkable to Nishiki and Gion. **Kyoto Station** is less charming but unbeatable for the Nara and Osaka legs. Higashiyama is lovely and costs half again as much. The ¥28,000 reflects a 30–40% foliage premium on the usual ¥18–20,000. Note **Kyoto's lodging tax rose 1 March 2026** — at this rate it's ¥400 pp/night, but it climbs steeply above ¥50,000/night.

**Osaka — 1 night, ~¥18,000.** **Namba** or Shinsaibashi: 5 minutes from Dōtonbori and on the direct Nankai line to KIX. Umeda works too but adds an airport transfer.

## Book ahead vs. turn up

Japan is mostly a turn-up country. The exceptions are short and worth respecting.

| When | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Now, 3+ months** | Open-jaw flights; Hakone ryokan; all three city hotels | November is peak. Kyoto is more competitive than it has ever been; good ryokan for late November go a year out. |
| **~1 month** | Shibuya Sky sunset slot; teamLab Borderless; Sagano Romantic Train; any high-end sushi or kaiseki | All timed-entry or counter-seated with hard caps. Sunset slots and foliage-season train seats vanish first. |
| **~1 month, optional** | Shinkansen, Romancecar, Kintetsu limited express seats | Reservations open 30 days out. Not strictly necessary mid-week, but cheap insurance with luggage. |
| **A few days out** | One or two nicer dinners per city | Small counters seat 8–12. Have the hotel call — many places don't take online or foreign bookings. |

**Just turn up:** every temple and shrine here — Sensō-ji, Meiji Jingū, Kiyomizu-dera, Fushimi Inari, Kinkaku-ji, Ryōan-ji, Nanzen-ji, Ginkaku-ji, Tenryū-ji, Tōdai-ji, Kasuga Taisha. Nishiki, Kuromon, and Tsukiji markets. Dōtonbori and every restaurant on it. Ramen, izakaya, conveyor sushi, department-store food halls. Tokyo National Museum, Hakone Open-Air Museum, Osaka Castle. The Eikan-dō night illumination (queue, don't book). Nara's deer.

**Two things people book and shouldn't:** the JR Pass, and guided day tours of Kyoto temples — Kyoto is trivially navigable alone, and tours lock you into the worst hours of the day.

## Practicalities

**Money.** More card-friendly than its reputation, but small restaurants, temples, shrines, and markets are cash only. Carry ¥30,000–40,000 and top up at **7-Eleven ATMs**, which reliably take foreign cards — bank ATMs often don't. Temple entry is ¥500–1,000 pp, cash.

**IC card — do this on arrival.** On **iPhone**, add **Welcome Suica Mobile** or Suica to Apple Wallet before leaving the airport; tops up with a foreign card via Apple Pay, with Mastercard and Amex most reliable (some foreign Visas fail). On **Android**, international handsets lack the FeliCa chip — get a **physical Welcome Suica** at the JR East Travel Service Center in Haneda Terminal 3. Note the physical card expires after 28 days and the remaining balance is **not refundable**, so don't over-load it. One card covers trains, buses, subways, lockers and convenience stores in every city here.

**Connectivity.** An **eSIM** is cheapest and simplest — $15–25 each for 10 days, activated before you fly. Pocket wifi only if a phone is incompatible. Google Maps works properly in Japan, down to live platforms and carriage numbers.

**November weather.** Tokyo and Kyoto roughly 8–17°C, dry and clear — the best weather of the year. Hakone is 5–8°C colder and can be fogged in; pack a warm layer for the ropeway. Kyoto mornings are cold enough that a 6am temple visit wants gloves. Bring shoes you can slip off easily and expect 15,000–20,000 steps a day.

**Small things.** No tipping, anywhere, ever. Don't eat while walking or talk on the phone on trains. Bins are scarce — carry a bag for your own litter. **Lunch is the value meal**: places charging ¥6,000 at dinner often serve the same food as a ¥1,500 lunch set, so eat your best meals at midday. Convenience-store food is genuinely good, not a compromise. **Tattoos** can bar you from public onsen — check the ryokan's policy or book a private bath.
